title: Panama — Ley 81 de 2019
subtitle: Discovery and masking of Panamanian personal data: cédula and RUC with a valid check digit, quasi-identifiers, the sensitive data of article 4, economic and credit data, and criminal records.

sections.title: About this profile set
body: This profile set finds the personal data in a Panamanian database and masks it, so that a non-production copy — for testing, development, training or analytics — no longer identifies anyone.
Masking only names and cédulas does not get there: a birth date, a sex and a small corregimiento are enough to point at one person. The set works on the same layers the risk is in:

list: **Direct identifiers** — cédula, RUC and its DV, names, contact, accounts and cards, passport and immigration documents, professional licenses, property, devices, vehicles, free text.
**Quasi-identifiers** — birth date, age, sex, district, corregimiento, barriada, postal code, occupation, employer, schooling.

**Sensitive data** — ethnic origin and indigenous language, health, biometric and genetic data, religious, philosophical and moral beliefs, political opinions and affiliation, union membership, sexual orientation.
**Economic and credit data** — APC credit references, debt, salary, assets, pensions, social security coverage, social programs, poverty, housing tenure.
**Criminal records** — police records and case numbers.

body: Everything the set needs travels with it: loading it creates the domains, classifiers, algorithms and lookup files, and sending it to a Masking Engine sends all of them.

sections.title: Law 81 of 2019 at a glance
body: Law 81 of 26 March 2019, on Personal Data Protection, was published in Gaceta Oficial 28743-A of 29 March 2019 and has been in force since 29 March 2021, two years after its enactment (art. 47). Executive Decree 285 of 28 May 2021 regulates it. The supervisory authority is the **National Authority for Transparency and Access to Information (ANTAI)**, through its Personal Data Protection Directorate.
What matters for a copy of production data:

list: **Personal data** is any information concerning natural persons that identifies them or makes them identifiable (art. 4, 9). The law protects natural persons: a legal entity's data is outside its scope.

**Sensitive data** is data that refers to the data subject's intimate sphere, or whose misuse may give rise to discrimination or carry a serious risk. As examples, not as a closed list, the law names data that may reveal racial or ethnic origin; religious, philosophical and moral beliefs or convictions; union membership; political opinions; data concerning health, life, sexual preference or orientation, genetic data or biometric data (art. 4, 11). Decree 285 defines biometric, genetic and health data (art. 4, 2 to 4).

**Anonymized data is out of scope.** Processing of information obtained through a prior dissociation or anonymization procedure, such that the result cannot be associated with the data subject, is excluded from the law (art. 3, 5). *Dissociated data* cannot be associated with the data subject nor, by its structure, content or level of detail, allow their identification (art. 4, 10).

**Purpose.** Data is used for the purposes it was authorized for; any other use needs consent, a special law or another legal basis (arts. 2, 2 and 11). Further processing for research or studies needs no consent when the data is anonymized (art. 12).

**Health and sensitive data.** Consent for health data must be prior, irrefutable and express (art. 8; Decree 285, art. 18). Sensitive data may not be transferred save for exceptions, and for historical, statistical or scientific purposes it must be dissociated (art. 13).
**Economic, financial, banking or commercial data** is processed with prior consent (art. 8, 3). Credit references also have a law of their own, Law 24 of 2002.
**Criminal convictions** have their own disclosure rules (art. 30; Decree 285, art. 7).

**Security.** Proportionate technical and organizational measures, especially for sensitive data (art. 2, 5; Decree 285, art. 36). A security breach is notified to ANTAI and to the affected data subjects within seventy-two hours (Decree 285, art. 37).

**Sanctions.** Fines from one thousand to ten thousand balboas set by ANTAI (art. 36). Disregarding the rules on sensitive data is a very serious infringement, which can lead to closing the database's records or suspending the processing activity (arts. 41 and 43).

body: A test environment with production data is processing for a purpose the data subject did not authorize, and it holds sensitive and financial data outside the controls built for them. A copy that is effectively anonymized falls, under article 3, outside the law: that is what the set is for.

The list of sensitive data is not exhaustive. The set also treats gender identity and sexual life as sensitive, since they expose people to discrimination in the same way. Reform proposals are under discussion, among them higher fines; this document follows the text in force in September 2026.

body.note: This document describes technical controls. Whether a copy counts as anonymized is a legal assessment of the whole environment — access, retention, what else it is combined with — not of the profile set alone.

sections.title: Using the set

list: **Load** — *Settings → Profile Sets → Load*. Loading again resets every object of the set to how it ships.
**Send to Delphix** — from the profile set, or with *Send everything to Delphix*. Domains, algorithms and files go first.
**Profile** — run a profiling job with the set and review the assigned domains before masking.
**Mask** — run the masking job. Use the same engine key in every environment so masked values stay consistent across systems.

body: The assignment threshold is 60%. An unambiguous column name reaches it alone; an ambiguous one — `NOMBRE`, `RESULTADO`, `CIUDAD` — needs the values to agree. A column with a meaningless name (`CAMPO1`, `OBS`) is still found when its values have a recognizable shape or vocabulary: a cédula, a RUC with its DV, a plate, a corregimiento.

Column names are recognized in Spanish, in the abbreviations of Panamanian systems (`NUM_CEDULA`, `CIP`, `FEC_NAC`, `COD_CORREG`, `NIS`), in the fields of the electronic invoice (`dRuc`, `dDV`) and in English.

body.tip: Before masking, inventory the binary columns (BLOBs, images, PDFs). Onboarding processes often store a photo of the cédula: the number is still readable in the image. Report those columns as residual risk.

groups.title: Direct identifiers
intro: Data that identifies a person on its own. The cédula is the key of almost every Panamanian record: it is a natural person's RUC, the number of their driver's license and their identification at the Social Security Fund. It is masked the same way everywhere, and the RUC keeps a valid check digit, because applications validate it.

groups.title: Quasi-identifiers
intro: Data that identifies no one on its own, but does in combination. Panama has 699 corregimientos, and 616 of them had fewer than 10,000 inhabitants in the 2023 census: a birth date, a sex and one of those corregimientos point at a handful of people. These attributes are generalized or shifted rather than replaced, and the data keeps its analytical value.

groups.title: Sensitive data
intro: The categories of article 4, section 11 — ethnic origin, health, genetic and biometric data, beliefs, political opinions, union membership, sexual orientation — and, because the list is not exhaustive, gender identity and sexual life. Categorical columns keep their shape: a yes/no flag stays a flag, a numeric code gets other digits and any other value is replaced by one from its category's list. Where the values share no vocabulary, they are suppressed to `Sin información`.

groups.title: Economic and credit data
intro: The law does not call them sensitive, but it requires prior consent for economic, financial, banking and commercial data (art. 8, 3), protects data subjects from automated decisions about their credit (art. 19), and credit references have a law of their own, Law 24 of 2002. They go beyond the bank account: an APC credit reference, a pension amount, a MIDES program or a poverty status say as much about a person as their salary. Categories are replaced within their own notation; amounts are mapped into a plausible range unrelated to the real value.

groups.title: Criminal records
intro: Criminal convictions have their own rules in the law (art. 30) and its regulation (Decree 285, art. 7), and are among the data most likely to give rise to discrimination. They get the same care as sensitive data.

PA_L1_CEDULA.title: Cédula (national ID)
PA_L1_CEDULA.what: The number of the identity card issued by the Electoral Tribunal: province of birth (1 to 13; 10, 11 and 12 are the Guna Yala, Emberá-Wounaan and Ngäbe-Buglé comarcas), tomo and asiento of the civil registry entry. `8-442-445`. Letters mark other cases: `E` resident foreigner, `N` naturalized, `PE` Panamanian born abroad, `AV` registered before the civil registry law, `PI` indigenous Panamanian; `8-NT-12-3456` is the tax number of someone without a cédula. In Panama the driver's license carries the cédula number, so license columns fall here too.
PA_L1_CEDULA.masking: The province becomes another province between 1 and 13, and tomo and asiento are mapped digit by digit keeping their length; the letters stay, and so does the document type. The mapping is one-to-one: a cédula used as a key does not collide. The same algorithm masks the cédula inside the RUC, so a person's cédula and RUC still agree. Text that is not shaped like a cédula is masked character by character.

PA_L1_RUC.title: RUC (taxpayer number)
PA_L1_RUC.what: The DGI's Single Taxpayer Registry number. A natural person's RUC is their cédula, with a two-digit check digit next to it: `8-442-445 DV 08`. A legal entity's RUC is its Public Registry number: `155596713-2-2015 DV 59`. One column often mixes both.
PA_L1_RUC.masking: A natural person's RUC is masked as their cédula and the DV is recomputed, so every masked RUC passes DGI validation. The separators ` DV `, ` DV`, `-` and a space are recognized. A legal entity's RUC stays as it is: it is not personal data under article 4, and keeping it keeps joins with supplier catalogs working. See *The RUC check digit, computed by the set*.

PA_L1_RUC_DV.title: DV in its own column
PA_L1_RUC_DV.what: The RUC check digit kept apart, as in the electronic invoice (`dDV`) or a `DV` column.
PA_L1_RUC_DV.masking: The two digits are mapped. They cannot be recomputed: an algorithm sees one column, and the RUC is in another. Masking it keeps it from helping link the row to the real RUC.

PA_L1_PASAPORTE.title: Passport
PA_L1_PASAPORTE.masking: Character by character, keeping length and format.

PA_L1_DOCUMENTO_MIGRATORIO.title: Immigration document
PA_L1_DOCUMENTO_MIGRATORIO.what: Resident cards, residence and work permits, visas and foreign identification numbers. A permanent resident's `E` cédula is in the cédula domain.
PA_L1_DOCUMENTO_MIGRATORIO.masking: Character by character, keeping length and format.

PA_L1_SEGURO_SOCIAL.title: Social security number
PA_L1_SEGURO_SOCIAL.what: The insured person's or card number of the Social Security Fund (CSS) kept by older systems. Today the CSS identifies the insured by their cédula.
PA_L1_SEGURO_SOCIAL.masking: Character by character, keeping length and format.

PA_L1_IDONEIDAD.title: Professional license (idoneidad)
PA_L1_IDONEIDAD.what: The idoneidad number that allows someone to practice a regulated profession — medicine, nursing, law, engineering. The registries are public: the number leads straight to the person's name.
PA_L1_IDONEIDAD.masking: Character by character, keeping the length.

PA_L1_NOMBRE.title: Given names
PA_L1_NOMBRE.what: First and middle names (`NOMBRES`, `PRIMER_NOMBRE`), including compound names such as `Luis Carlos`.
PA_L1_NOMBRE.masking: Each word is replaced by a name from a list of 253 names used in Panama, keeping the number of words and the case. More than three words are masked character by character.

PA_L1_APELLIDO.title: Surnames
PA_L1_APELLIDO.what: Paternal and maternal surnames, in one column or two, and a married woman's surname: `González de Pérez`.
PA_L1_APELLIDO.masking: Each surname is replaced by one from a list of 200 surnames common in Panama — led by Rodríguez, González, Sánchez, Martínez, Castillo and Ábrego —, keeping the number of words and the case. The `de` of a married surname stays.

PA_L1_NOMBRE_COMPLETO.title: Full name
PA_L1_NOMBRE_COMPLETO.what: Given names and surnames in one column, in Panamanian order, with `de` and the husband's surname where present, or as `APELLIDOS, NOMBRES`. Also the name of an account holder, beneficiary, insured person or guardian (*acudiente*).
PA_L1_NOMBRE_COMPLETO.masking: Given names become given names and surnames become surnames, by position: one word is a given name, two are a given name and a surname, three are a given name and two surnames, four are two given names and two surnames. `María Elena González de Pérez` keeps its `de` and its structure. A comma separates surnames from given names.

PA_L1_EMAIL.title: E-mail
PA_L1_EMAIL.masking: The name and domain are mapped character by character and the top-level domain becomes `.test`, reserved for testing: a masked address never receives mail.

PA_L1_TELEFONO.title: Phone
PA_L1_TELEFONO.what: Seven-digit landlines (`223-4567`) and eight-digit mobiles starting with 6 (`6123-4567`), with or without `+507`. Panama has no area codes.
PA_L1_TELEFONO.masking: `+507`, the separators and the first digit — the 6 of a mobile, the region of a landline — stay; the rest is masked digit by digit. A number not shaped like a Panamanian number is masked whole.

PA_L1_DIRECCION.title: Address
PA_L1_DIRECCION.what: The address line as written in Panama, which rarely has a street number: street or road, building, floor and apartment, or barriada, street and house.
PA_L1_DIRECCION.masking: It is replaced by one of 3,000 fictitious Panamanian addresses, with common streets, roads, barriadas and buildings in realistic proportions.

PA_L1_DIRECCION_COMPLEMENTO.title: Address detail
PA_L1_DIRECCION_COMPLEMENTO.what: House, apartment, floor, building, tower or lot numbers in columns of their own.
PA_L1_DIRECCION_COMPLEMENTO.masking: Character by character, keeping length and format.

PA_L1_CUENTA_BANCARIA.title: Bank account
PA_L1_CUENTA_BANCARIA.what: Checking, savings and payroll account numbers, in each bank's formats.
PA_L1_CUENTA_BANCARIA.masking: Character by character, keeping length and format.

PA_L1_TARJETA.title: Payment card
PA_L1_TARJETA.what: Credit, debit and prepaid card numbers, including the Tarjeta Clave Social through which MIDES pays its programs.
PA_L1_TARJETA.masking: Replaced by another card number that still passes the Luhn check. Values not shaped like a card pass unchanged instead of failing the row.

PA_L1_IP.title: IP address
PA_L1_IP.what: IPv4 and IPv6 addresses of users and devices.
PA_L1_IP.masking: Each IPv4 octet is mapped to a number from 1 to 254; an IPv6 address is mapped as hexadecimal.

PA_L1_DISPOSITIVO.title: Device identifier
PA_L1_DISPOSITIVO.what: IMEI, MAC address, advertising and session identifiers, equipment serial numbers.
PA_L1_DISPOSITIVO.masking: Hex stays hex and digits stay digits, so the value keeps its format.

PA_L1_PLACA.title: License plate
PA_L1_PLACA.what: Plates in the format used since 2013, two letters and four digits (`AB1234`), the earlier six-digit ones, and category plates: `M` motorcycle, `T` taxi, `B` bus, `G` government, `CD` diplomatic corps, `PR` press and others.
PA_L1_PLACA.masking: Serial letters and digits are mapped; category letters stay, so a taxi plate is still a taxi plate.

PA_L1_VIN.title: Vehicle identification number
PA_L1_VIN.what: The VIN, and engine and chassis numbers.
PA_L1_VIN.masking: Character by character, keeping length and format.

PA_L1_FINCA.title: Property number (finca)
PA_L1_FINCA.what: A property's finca number, folio real or cadastral location code. The Public Registry can be searched by anyone: the finca leads to its owner.
PA_L1_FINCA.masking: Character by character, keeping length and format.

PA_L1_NUMERO_CONTRATO.title: Contract or customer number
PA_L1_NUMERO_CONTRATO.what: Contract, policy, loan, customer, employee, payroll or claim numbers, and the electricity service's NIS.
PA_L1_NUMERO_CONTRATO.masking: Character by character, keeping length and format.

PA_L1_USUARIO_RRSS.title: User name or social network
PA_L1_USUARIO_RRSS.what: User names, aliases and social network profiles.
PA_L1_USUARIO_RRSS.masking: Character by character, keeping length and format.

PA_L1_CREDENCIAL.title: Credential
PA_L1_CREDENCIAL.what: Passwords, PINs, password hashes, tokens and API keys.
PA_L1_CREDENCIAL.masking: Every character becomes `X`. A credential has no reason to look real in a test environment.

PA_L1_GEOLOCALIZACION.title: Geolocation
PA_L1_GEOLOCALIZACION.what: Latitude and longitude, together or in separate columns. Panama lies between 7° and 10° north and 77° and 83° west.
PA_L1_GEOLOCALIZACION.masking: The integer part and first decimal stay — about 11 km — and the rest is masked: the place is generalized, not moved.

PA_L1_TEXTO_LIBRE.title: Free text
PA_L1_TEXTO_LIBRE.what: Remarks, comments, complaints and notes where personal data is written without structure.
PA_L1_TEXTO_LIBRE.masking: Free Text Redaction: cédulas, e-mails, mobiles, hyphenated landlines, card numbers, plates and IPs become `[DATO]`, and the given names and surnames of the lists become `[NOMBRE]`.

PA_L2_FECHA_NACIMIENTO.title: Birth date
PA_L2_FECHA_NACIMIENTO.what: The birth date, in date, timestamp or text columns.
PA_L2_FECHA_NACIMIENTO.masking: Shifted up to 60 days back or forward: it breaks the link to the person and keeps ages and cohorts almost intact.

PA_L2_ANIO_NACIMIENTO.title: Birth year
PA_L2_ANIO_NACIMIENTO.masking: The decade stays and the last digit is mapped: 1985 becomes another year of the eighties.

PA_L2_EDAD.title: Age
PA_L2_EDAD.what: Ages in years, whole or with decimals.
PA_L2_EDAD.masking: The tens digit stays and the units digit is mapped (37 becomes 3x). From 100 on, 90: extreme ages identify on their own.

PA_L2_FECHA_EVENTO.title: Life event dates
PA_L2_FECHA_EVENTO.what: Dates of death, marriage, hiring and leaving a job, retirement, hospitalization, diagnosis, naturalization and other personal events.
PA_L2_FECHA_EVENTO.masking: Shifted up to 30 days: less than the birth date, since they are often combined with it.

PA_L2_SEXO.title: Sex
PA_L2_SEXO.masking: Replaced within its own vocabulary: `F`/`M` stays `F`/`M`.

PA_L2_DISTRITO.title: District
PA_L2_DISTRITO.what: The district name. Panama has 81 inhabited districts — the Guna Yala comarca is not divided into districts —, and 47 had fewer than 20,000 inhabitants in 2023.
PA_L2_DISTRITO.masking: A district under 20,000 inhabitants becomes the nearest district of its province or comarca with at least 20,000; larger ones stay. See *Where people live*.

PA_L2_CORREGIMIENTO.title: Corregimiento
PA_L2_CORREGIMIENTO.what: The corregimiento name, the smallest division with a census population: 699 of them, averaging 5,800 inhabitants.
PA_L2_CORREGIMIENTO.masking: A corregimiento under 10,000 inhabitants becomes the nearest corregimiento of its province or comarca with at least 10,000, or of the country if the province has none. Large ones stay. See *Where people live*.

PA_L2_CODIGO_LUGAR.title: Corregimiento or district code
PA_L2_CODIGO_LUGAR.what: INEC geographic codes: six digits for a corregimiento (`040612`), four for a district (`0306`), also without the leading zero.
PA_L2_CODIGO_LUGAR.masking: By the same rule as the names: a small corregimiento or district becomes the code of the large one it maps to.

PA_L2_LUGAR_POBLADO.title: Populated place
PA_L2_LUGAR_POBLADO.what: Populated places, hamlets and communities, and the place of birth.
PA_L2_LUGAR_POBLADO.masking: Replaced by the name of a corregimiento of more than 20,000 inhabitants: still a place, no longer theirs.

PA_L2_BARRIADA.title: Barriada or neighborhood
PA_L2_BARRIADA.what: Barriadas, urbanizaciones, residential developments and sectors.
PA_L2_BARRIADA.masking: Replaced by one of 75 common barriadas and neighborhoods.

PA_L2_CODIGO_POSTAL.title: Postal code
PA_L2_CODIGO_POSTAL.what: Postal codes of Correos y Telégrafos, little used in Panama. The first two digits give the province.
PA_L2_CODIGO_POSTAL.masking: The first two digits stay and the rest becomes zeros.

PA_L2_NACIONALIDAD.title: Nationality
PA_L2_NACIONALIDAD.what: Nationality or country of birth. In a Panamanian database, an uncommon nationality identifies.
PA_L2_NACIONALIDAD.masking: Replaced by one of the 20 most common nationalities in Panama.

PA_L2_ESTADO_CIVIL.title: Marital status
PA_L2_ESTADO_CIVIL.what: Marital status, in the census categories: in a union, married, single, separated from a marriage, separated from a union, divorced, widowed.
PA_L2_ESTADO_CIVIL.masking: Replaced by another of the seven categories.

PA_L2_OCUPACION.title: Occupation
PA_L2_OCUPACION.what: Occupation, profession or job title. A rare title (`Gerente Regional de Operaciones Bocas del Toro`) is unique in the database.
PA_L2_OCUPACION.masking: Replaced by one of 40 common occupations.

PA_L2_EMPLEADOR.title: Employer
PA_L2_EMPLEADOR.what: The name of the employer (*patrono*) or workplace.
PA_L2_EMPLEADOR.masking: Replaced by one of 25 fictitious employers.

PA_L2_ESCOLARIDAD.title: Schooling
PA_L2_ESCOLARIDAD.what: Education level in the terms of the Panamanian system: primaria, premedia, media, vocational, higher education.
PA_L2_ESCOLARIDAD.masking: Replaced by another of the 13 levels.

PA_L2_ESCUELA.title: School
PA_L2_ESCUELA.what: The name of the school, colegio, basic education center or university.
PA_L2_ESCUELA.masking: Replaced by one of 15 fictitious schools.

PA_L2_DEPENDIENTES.title: Children and dependents
PA_L2_DEPENDIENTES.what: Number of children, dependents or household members.
PA_L2_DEPENDIENTES.masking: Capped at 5: large households are rare, and a rare count identifies.

PA_L3_ETNIA.title: Ethnic origin
PA_L3_ETNIA.what: Belonging to an indigenous people — Ngäbe, Guna, Emberá, Buglé, Wounaan, Naso Tjërdi, Bokota, Bri Bri — or Afro-descendant self-identification — Afro-Panamanian, moreno, black, Afro-colonial, Afro-Antillean —, in the terms of the 2023 census, often as a yes/no flag.
PA_L3_ETNIA.masking: A flag stays a flag in its vocabulary, a code gets other digits and any other value is replaced by one from the census list.

PA_L3_LENGUA_INDIGENA.title: Indigenous language
PA_L3_LENGUA_INDIGENA.what: The indigenous language the person speaks: Ngäbere, Buglere, Guna, Emberá, Wounmeu, Naso Tjërdi, Bribri.
PA_L3_LENGUA_INDIGENA.masking: Like ethnic origin: flags and codes keep their shape, names are replaced by another language from the list.

PA_L3_SALUD_DIAGNOSTICO.title: Diagnosis
PA_L3_SALUD_DIAGNOSTICO.what: Diagnoses, as ICD-10 codes (`F32.9`, `B20`) or text, and medical history, allergies and chronic conditions.
PA_L3_SALUD_DIAGNOSTICO.masking: An ICD-10 code is replaced by another common code of the same format, with or without a decimal; text, by a common diagnosis. The real diagnosis does not survive.

PA_L3_SALUD_MEDICAMENTO.title: Medication
PA_L3_SALUD_MEDICAMENTO.what: Medications and active ingredients. Some reveal the diagnosis: an antiretroviral, an antipsychotic.
PA_L3_SALUD_MEDICAMENTO.masking: Replaced by one of 26 common medications.

PA_L3_SALUD_IDENTIFICADOR.title: Clinical identifier
PA_L3_SALUD_IDENTIFICADOR.what: Medical record, file, admission, prescription or sick-leave number.
PA_L3_SALUD_IDENTIFICADOR.masking: Character by character, keeping length and format.

PA_L3_SALUD_TEXTO_CLINICO.title: Clinical text
PA_L3_SALUD_TEXTO_CLINICO.what: Progress notes, medical history, discharge summaries and clinical summaries.
PA_L3_SALUD_TEXTO_CLINICO.masking: Free Text Redaction, as for free text: cédulas, contact details and names are redacted. The clinical content stays; if it must go too, assign the column to a suppression domain.

PA_L3_SALUD_RESULTADO_EXAMEN.title: Test result
PA_L3_SALUD_RESULTADO_EXAMEN.what: Laboratory and imaging results: HIV, viral load, glucose, pregnancy or drug tests.
PA_L3_SALUD_RESULTADO_EXAMEN.masking: Character by character, keeping length and format.

PA_L3_SALUD_GRUPO_SANGUINEO.title: Blood group
PA_L3_SALUD_GRUPO_SANGUINEO.masking: Replaced by another of the eight groups.

PA_L3_SALUD_DISCAPACIDAD.title: Disability
PA_L3_SALUD_DISCAPACIDAD.what: Type or degree of disability, in the types SENADIS certifies: physical, visual, hearing, intellectual, psychosocial, visceral.
PA_L3_SALUD_DISCAPACIDAD.masking: Flags and codes keep their shape; the type is replaced by another from the list.

PA_L3_SALUD_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTIVA.title: Sexual and reproductive health
PA_L3_SALUD_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTIVA.what: Pregnancy, weeks of gestation, abortions, contraception, fertility, sexually transmitted infections.
PA_L3_SALUD_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTIVA.masking: Flags keep their shape; any other value becomes `Sin información`.

PA_L3_SALUD_MENTAL_ADICCIONES.title: Mental health and addiction
PA_L3_SALUD_MENTAL_ADICCIONES.what: Mental disorders, suicide attempts, substance use and addiction treatment.

PA_L3_BIOMETRICO.title: Biometric data
PA_L3_BIOMETRICO.what: Fingerprint, face, iris or voice templates stored as text (hash, base64). The law names them sensitive and Decree 285 defines them.
PA_L3_BIOMETRICO.masking: Every character becomes `X`. Binary columns are out of reach: see *Limits*.

PA_L3_INFORMACION_GENETICA.title: Genetic data
PA_L3_INFORMACION_GENETICA.what: Genetic profiles, sequences, mutations, karyotypes, paternity tests.

PA_L3_ORIENTACION_SEXUAL.title: Sexual orientation
PA_L3_ORIENTACION_SEXUAL.what: Sexual orientation or preference, which the law names explicitly.
PA_L3_ORIENTACION_SEXUAL.masking: Flags and codes keep their shape; the value is replaced by another from the list.

PA_L3_IDENTIDAD_GENERO.title: Gender identity
PA_L3_IDENTIDAD_GENERO.what: Gender identity, name changes for identity, pronouns.
PA_L3_IDENTIDAD_GENERO.masking: Flags and codes keep their shape; the value is replaced by another from the list.

PA_L3_RELIGION.title: Religion
PA_L3_RELIGION.what: Religion or denomination: Catholic, Evangelical, Adventist, Jehovah's Witness, Bahá'í, Jewish, Muslim, and the indigenous religions Mamatata and Ibeorgun.
PA_L3_RELIGION.masking: Flags and codes keep their shape; the value is replaced by another from the list.

PA_L3_CREENCIA_FILOSOFICA_MORAL.title: Philosophical and moral beliefs
PA_L3_CREENCIA_FILOSOFICA_MORAL.what: Personal convictions, conscientious objection, ethical positions.

PA_L3_OPINION_POLITICA.title: Political opinion
PA_L3_OPINION_POLITICA.masking: Replaced by another position on a generic scale.

PA_L3_AFILIACION_POLITICA.title: Political affiliation
PA_L3_AFILIACION_POLITICA.what: The party a person is registered with or supports. The Electoral Tribunal counted more than 1.5 million party members in 2026.
PA_L3_AFILIACION_POLITICA.masking: Replaced by one of the legally constituted parties — PRD, Realizando Metas, Cambio Democrático, Panameñista, MOLIRENA, MOCA, FAD, Alianza, Partido Popular — or by independent candidacy (*libre postulación*) or no party.

PA_L3_AFILIACION_SINDICAL.title: Union membership
PA_L3_AFILIACION_SINDICAL.what: Membership of a union, guild or workers' association, union dues, collective agreement.
PA_L3_AFILIACION_SINDICAL.masking: Flags keep their shape; any other value becomes `Sin información`.

PA_FIN_REFERENCIA_CREDITO.title: Credit reference
PA_FIN_REFERENCIA_CREDITO.what: APC scores and references, days past due, delinquent portfolio, collection lawsuits, written-off accounts.
PA_FIN_REFERENCIA_CREDITO.masking: A score gets other digits, a flag stays a flag and any status is replaced by another credit status.

PA_FIN_MONTO_DEUDA.title: Debt amount
PA_FIN_MONTO_DEUDA.what: Balances of loans, cards and mortgages, past-due amounts, credit limits, installments.
PA_FIN_MONTO_DEUDA.masking: Mapped to an amount between B/.100 and B/.500,000.

PA_FIN_INGRESO_MENSUAL.title: Salary and income
PA_FIN_INGRESO_MENSUAL.masking: Mapped to an amount between B/.350 and B/.25,000.

PA_FIN_PATRIMONIO.title: Assets
PA_FIN_PATRIMONIO.what: Cadastral or market value of real estate and vehicles, savings, term deposits, net worth.
PA_FIN_PATRIMONIO.masking: Mapped to an amount between B/.10,000 and B/.3,000,000.

PA_FIN_PENSION.title: Pension and individual account
PA_FIN_PENSION.what: CSS retirement or pension amount, balance of the individual account, of SIACAP or of the severance fund.
PA_FIN_PENSION.masking: Mapped to an amount between B/.120 and B/.6,000.

PA_FIN_SEGURO_SOCIAL.title: Social security coverage
PA_FIN_SEGURO_SOCIAL.what: A person's standing with the Social Security Fund, in the census categories: direct insured, beneficiary, retired or pensioner, no social security. It reveals formal or informal work.
PA_FIN_SEGURO_SOCIAL.masking: Flags and codes keep their shape; the category is replaced by another.

PA_FIN_PROGRAMA_SOCIAL.title: Social program
PA_FIN_PROGRAMA_SOCIAL.what: Beneficiaries of transfer programs: MIDES's 120 a los 65, Red de Oportunidades, Ángel Guardián and Bono Alimenticio Nutricional, IFARHU's PASE-U and scholarships. Being a beneficiary reveals poverty, old age or disability.
PA_FIN_PROGRAMA_SOCIAL.masking: Flags and codes keep their shape; the program is replaced by another.

PA_FIN_NIVEL_SOCIOECONOMICO.title: Socioeconomic level
PA_FIN_NIVEL_SOCIOECONOMICO.what: Poverty status, income quintile or decile, multidimensional poverty index.
PA_FIN_NIVEL_SOCIOECONOMICO.masking: A quintile or decile becomes another number of the same range, with its prefix; a status, another from the list.

PA_FIN_VIVIENDA.title: Housing tenure
PA_FIN_VIVIENDA.what: Whether the home is owned, mortgaged, rented, lent or an informal settlement, and its conditions.
PA_FIN_VIVIENDA.masking: Flags and codes keep their shape; the tenure is replaced by another from the census list.

PA_PENAL_ANTECEDENTES.title: Criminal record
PA_PENAL_ANTECEDENTES.what: Police record (*récord policivo*), criminal record, sentences, offences, detentions and precautionary measures.
PA_PENAL_ANTECEDENTES.masking: A flag stays a flag; any other value becomes a generic status: with a record, without a record, or no information.

PA_PENAL_CAUSA.title: Case number
PA_PENAL_CAUSA.what: Case file (*carpetilla*), investigation folder, case, court file or complaint numbers.
PA_PENAL_CAUSA.masking: Character by character, keeping length and format.

closing.title: The RUC check digit, computed by the set
body: A natural person's RUC check digit is two digits that the DGI computes over a 21-position table: the cédula fields right-aligned in fixed widths — asiento 5, tomo 3, a two-digit code for the letters (`AV` 15, `PI` 79, `E` 50, `N` 40, `PE` 75), province 2 — and a constant 5. Weights grow from 2 at the right, modulo 11, and a remainder of 0 or 1 gives 0; the second digit repeats the computation with the first one appended. A field longer than its width pushes the fields to its left, and a one-digit province with `AV` or `PI` is padded with two zeros.
No framework of the plugin does this: Check Digit can add weighted digits, but not pad fields or weigh letters. The set does it with tables:

list: The cédula is masked with the same algorithm as the cédula domain. Letters and separators are swapped for one-character markers, and the old DV is replaced by an initial state.

The state — weighted sum, digit sum and position — travels through the value from right to left, one character per step. Each step is a Data Cleansing that turns *character + state* into *new state + character*.
At the left end, a table turns the state into the two digits of the DV, and a second pass carries them back to where the old DV was.
The markers become letters and separators again.

body: The tables are Data Cleansing files generated with the set, and the steps are Regex Decompose algorithms joined in String Algorithm Chains of at most eight — the engine's limit. Every masked RUC has a valid DV and the mapping stays one-to-one. The price is a long algorithm tree under the domain and a step table of more than 30,000 lines.

closing.title: Where people live: districts and corregimientos
body: With the data of the 2023 XII Population Census (INEC), the set knows the population, district, province and location of each of the 699 corregimientos.

list: A **corregimiento** under 10,000 inhabitants becomes the nearest corregimiento of its province or comarca with at least 10,000. Darién, Los Santos and the Emberá-Wounaan and Ngäbe-Buglé comarcas have none: theirs become the nearest one in the country.
A **district** under 20,000 inhabitants becomes the nearest district of its province or comarca with at least 20,000, or of the country in the Emberá-Wounaan comarca.
Distance is measured between centroids, a district's weighted by the population of its corregimientos.
Sixty corregimiento names repeat — there are five San José —: a name is generalized only when every place bearing it is small. INEC codes have no such ambiguity.

body: The result is always a real place, near the original, and every group of people who end up sharing a name holds at least 10,000 inhabitants. Names that are also given names or surnames are left out of the detection list, so that a surname column is not taken for corregimientos.

list: **Binary columns** — photos of the cédula, fingerprint images, clinical PDFs in BLOBs — cannot be masked by these algorithms. Inventory them and report them as residual risk.
**A DV in its own column** is not recomputed: it is masked, and no longer matches the masked RUC. Where the application validates a RUC and DV stored separately, validation fails.

**The cédula letters stay.** `PI` still marks a registration as an indigenous Panamanian, and `E`, `N` and `PE` the status of foreigner, naturalized or born abroad. Changing them would break the format or make different cédulas collide. If that is sensitive in your case, handle it together with the ethnic origin or nationality column.
**Cédulas with a zero-padded province** (`08-442-445`) or without hyphens are masked character by character, without recomputing the DV. An `NT` RUC is also masked without recomputing.
**A legal entity's RUC stays.** A company with a single owner is still a legal entity under the law.
**Data Cleansing leaves unknown values as they are**: a corregimiento spelled in a way the list does not have passes unchanged.
**Free text** is redacted token by token: a phone written with spaces is not found, and a given name that is also a common word (`Luz`, `Rosa`) is redacted wherever it appears.
**Minors** — a birth date moves at most 60 days, so few people cross their 18th birthday, but some do. Where that matters, split the rule by age group with Multi-Column Condition.
**Addresses** are replaced as a whole line. Street, barriada, corregimiento and district in separate columns are masked independently and no longer form a coherent address.
**Plates and VINs** keep their format, but not the VIN check digit.

closing.title: Verification
body: The set is generated and checked by two scripts kept next to it in the repository:

list: `build.mjs` generates the set, its lookup tables and the DV tables from the definitions and the hand-kept lists.

`verify.mjs` first confirms that its DV computation reproduces the examples of the published algorithm. It reviews every classifier configuration and profiles 138 columns with the whole set at its threshold — well named, badly named and 24 that are not personal data. It then masks 255 sample values and 210 placeholders such as `N/D` through the running app: RUCs with a DV in the four separators and the five letter types, checking each DV; 150 cédulas and 150 RUCs for collisions; and 20 people whose cédula and RUC must still agree.

body: In the last build, every column was assigned as expected and every value was masked as expected.

list: Law 81 of 26 March 2019, on Personal Data Protection — Gaceta Oficial 28743-A, 29 March 2019 (National Assembly, Legispan).
Executive Decree 285 of 28 May 2021, regulating Law 81 of 2019.
National Authority for Transparency and Access to Information (ANTAI), Personal Data Protection Directorate.
Algorithm for the RUC check digit — Dirección General de Ingresos and the National Authority for Government Innovation.
Format of the cédula and its letters — Electoral Tribunal, National Directorate of Identity Cards. Party membership, July and August 2026 — Electoral Tribunal.

Population, code and location of the 699 corregimientos; indigenous and Afro-descendant groups; marital status; social security; schooling — XII National Population and VIII Housing Census 2023 (INEC), in the geographic service by corregimiento published with Esri Panamá.
Most frequent surnames and given names — Civil Registry of the Electoral Tribunal.
Certified disability types — National Secretariat for Disability (SENADIS). Transfer programs, 2026 — Ministry of Social Development (MIDES) and IFARHU (PASE-U).

Credit references — Law 24 of 2002 and APC. Religion — 2015 national survey. Plates — Land Transit and Transport Authority (2013 format). Phone numbering — ASEP, National Numbering Plan. Postal codes — Correos y Telégrafos.
